findings.title: Document the actual SLA discriminator and null semantics
findings.failure: The tool descriptions say `__typename` is `Pending`, `Breaching`, etc. and that a target is null whenever it does not apply. The payload actually contains full GraphQL type names such as `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending`. It can also contain `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailCancelled` after the target stops matching the thread. An MCP consumer following the documented contract can fail to classify the status or incorrectly treat cancellation as impossible for a non-applicable target.
findings.fix: List the exact `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail*` typename values. Define null as meaning no tracker was returned, and explicitly state that the latest tracker can be `Cancelled` after the SLA stops applying.
findings.evidence: The union members are named `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailPending` through `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetailCancelled` in `packages/core-graphql/src/schema.ts:14112`, and `resolveServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail` returns those exact names. `lambdas/core-graphql-api/src/threads/changeThreadPriorityMutation.slas.litest.ts:463` expects a cancelled first-response tracker after a priority change makes the prior SLA inapplicable. The GraphQL October 2021 specification §4.1 defines `__typename` as the object type name.

findings.title: Use operation-local fragments for the repeated SLA selection
findings.failure: The same union selection is copied four times per operation and twelve times overall. A future status or timestamp-field change can update only some targets or tools, silently producing inconsistent MCP response shapes.
findings.fix: In each file, define a uniquely named fragment such as `GetThreadsSlaStatusDetail` on `ServiceLevelAgreementStatusDetail`, then spread it under all four targets. Operation-local fragments are already used by `searchBroadcasts.graphql`, `getBroadcastDetails.graphql`, and other MCP operations.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide search `rg '^fragment ' services/mcp-server/operations` proves the loader already supports this pattern. The PR adds 561 lines, primarily twelve copies of the same roughly 44-line selection.

checked_fine: Deploy: all three operation files are copied into the MCP Docker asset, and `ecs.ContainerImage.fromAsset('services/mcp-server')` changes the task definition when they change; no environment variables, permissions, exports, imports, or OpenTofu resources changed.

Contract parity: every pre-existing variable, filter, route, auth setting, sort, pagination field, and response selection remains unchanged. The added SLA enum/type names and timestamp fields match the existing base GraphQL schema.

Filter defaults: omitted `slaStatuses` and `slaTypes` become null; `ThreadsFilter` accepts the all-null `serviceLevelAgreements` object and `threadDbFilterUtils` emits no SLA predicate when it contains no conditions.

Resolver behavior: list and search results use `serviceLevelAgreementTrackerDataLoader`, which batches all thread IDs into one aggregate query rather than introducing an N+1. Threads with neither a tier nor an SLA policy return four nulls without that query.

Data and rollback: there are no migrations, stored-schema changes, deletes, retention changes, or one-way state transitions. Rolling back removes only the additive MCP fields and filters; the underlying GraphQL schema predates this PR.
Blast radius: no shared constants, aggregates, schemas, resolver behavior, events, or infrastructure were modified; behavior changes are limited to the three public MCP operations.

Dead code: repo-wide searches for the operation names and `serviceLevelAgreementStatusSummary` show all additions are reachable through `mcp.config.yaml`'s `/data/operations/` loader, the Docker `COPY operations/`, and the deployed ECS image.

Output parity: all four SLA targets select all six existing union variants with their matching fields—pending/imminent breach times and pause data, breaching time, achieved time, breached/completed times, and cancellation time.
Static hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1 HEAD` passed. No deployed e2e or contract tests were run.
